system.name: SlimWiFi
system.one_liner: an ultra-low-power IoT radio architecture enabled by asymmetric communication

components.role: high-resolution digital-to-analog converter supporting complex modulation

components.role: crystal oscillator reference for the carrier generator

components.name: PLL+VCO

components.name: Mixer
components.role: mixes the baseband signal with the carrier

components.name: OOK Modulation
components.role: on-off-keying modulation applied via an RF switch, replacing the DAC

content.key_idea: Because SlimWiFi only needs low transmit power, low-accuracy carrier frequency, and simple on-off keying, it strips the power-hungry DAC and closed-loop PLL+VCO that a traditional active transmitter requires.

summary: Figure 12 contrasts two transmitter hardware designs as circuit schematics. Panel (a) shows a traditional active transmitter: a DAC and a crystal-oscillator-referenced PLL+VCO carrier generator feed a Mixer, whose output drives a high-power PA before the antenna. Panel (b) shows the SlimWiFi active transmitter proposed by the paper, which removes the DAC and mixer in favor of directly gating a simple Open-loop oscillator with an RF switch to produce an OOK-modulated signal, which then drives a much lower-power (-20 dBm) PA. The comparison visually argues that SlimWiFi's asymmetric-communication design, needing only low transmit power, low-accuracy carrier frequency, and simple on-off keying, lets it strip out the power-hungry DAC and closed-loop frequency synthesis that traditional IoT radios require. Both panels are drawn as plain black-and-white circuit schematics with no color coding.
summary_zh: 图12对比两种发射机：(a)传统方案含DAC、锁相环与Mixer驱动高功率PA；(b)SlimWiFi省去DAC和Mixer，用开环振荡器加RF开关产生OOK信号驱动低功率PA，体现硬件精简。
